title: Monday Morning Quarterback
date_line: Tuesday, Oct. 20, 2026. Weekend review. College Saturday (Oct. 17) and all of NFL Week 6, Monday night included, graded. Then next weekend, with the new numbers.

paragraphs: Every pick below is graded against the line printed on its card when the game kicked off, not the closing line. A push counts as neither a hit nor a miss.

What got graded: 52 college games from Saturday and 13 NFL games, Sunday's 12 plus Monday night. College cards carried a side from the Cover Writer and from each handicapper, plus a Cover Writer total. NFL cards carried whatever each card actually showed at kickoff.

What did not get graded: Thursday's NFL game (Seattle 14 at Denver 17, overtime), Thursday's college games (East Carolina 17 at UAB 30, overtime; Georgia Southern 23 at Old Dominion 15; Colorado State 27 at Texas State 66) and Friday's college games (Memphis 17 at Tulane 31, Washington 38 at Purdue 26, Appalachian State 35 at Coastal Carolina 32). Three FCS-opponent games (The Citadel at Texas A&M, Charleston Southern at Clemson, Elon at Stanford) had no pick. In the NFL, a handicapper is graded only where its card showed a team or an Over/Under at kickoff. Where a card showed neither, there is nothing to grade.
Monday night is final, so the whole weekend is graded. It leads off both parts.
Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches, all on San Francisco −7.5 (card line). San Francisco won by 6. Missed by 1.5.
Card case: this was The Formula's widest gap of the week. The Formula: Net ratings 49ers 9.8, Commanders −9.1 (nflverse play-by-play, Oct. 18, 2026).
Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches all had San Francisco −7.5 too, and the Cover Writer's card read 49ers 35, Commanders 16.
The card's own story flagged the danger: the number sat a half-point past 7, so a 49ers win by exactly 7 would land on Washington's side. The 49ers came up even shorter than that.

For most of three quarters, nobody was sweating. Christian McCaffrey scored twice from a yard out, the second with 13 seconds left in the half, for a 20-3 lead. Eddy Pineiro's 33-yard field goal made it 23-3 with 5:56 left in the third. San Francisco was covering by 12.5.

The 49ers had already left points out there. Pineiro missed the extra point after McCaffrey's first touchdown, wide right, so it was 13-3 instead of 14-3. In the second quarter, McCaffrey made a catch at the Washington 21 and fumbled, and Frankie Luvu recovered at the 19. The field-goal drive in the third stalled at the Washington 14 on a third-and-3 incompletion.
Then Washington came back. Facing fourth-and-5 at the San Francisco 31, Jayden Daniels hit Stefon Diggs for 13 yards. Diggs caught a 1-yard touchdown with 15 seconds left in the third: 23-10.

The next Washington drive killed the cover, and San Francisco flags kept it moving. On third-and-4 at the Washington 26, an incompletion became a first down on illegal contact against R. Green. On third-and-8 at the San Francisco 41, Antonio Williams made a 23-yard catch, and roughing the passer on Osa Odighizuwa moved the ball to the 9. On the next snap, Daniels threw a 9-yard touchdown to Rachaad White: 23-17 with 9:22 left.

That made it a 6-point game, and San Francisco −7.5 needed one more score. It never came. The 49ers' last three possessions all ended in punts, two of them stalled by sacks of Brock Purdy from Shy Tuttle and Odafe Oweh. San Francisco did not score after the 5:56 mark of the third quarter.
Put Pineiro's missed extra point back and it is a 7-point win, still a half-point short.

The 49ers almost lost it outright. Their last punt came after a delay of game, and a fair-catch interference penalty on Siran Neal handed Washington the ball at its own 46. Daniels got the Commanders to the San Francisco 28 with 22 seconds left. Then came an intentional-grounding penalty with a 10-second runoff and an 18-yard sack by Keion White and Romello Height on the last snap.
Follow The Money is the one card that never laid the 7.5. It gets no credit for that, but it did not get burned either.
Missed: Follow The Money on Over 52 (card total). The final total was 40. Missed by 12.
Card case: Follow The Money saw the total open at 50.5 and climb to 52, a 1.5-point move, and it went Over. It was the only card on the Over. The other four had the Under.

It was 33 points after three quarters, so the Over needed 20 more in the fourth. The fourth produced 7. The biggest near-miss came with 4:19 left, when Jeremy McNichols ran 31 yards for a touchdown that would have tied it, and a face-mask penalty on C. Paul wiped it out. Washington got another life when a fourth-and-8 sack was erased by illegal contact on Ashtyn Davis. Then Daniels threw incomplete to Treylon Burks on fourth-and-3 at the San Francisco 17 with 2:00 left.

Even with McNichols' touchdown and an extra point, the total would have been 47, still 5 points under 52. Follow The Money took on the other four cards on this total and lost that argument by 12 points.
Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula and Follow The Money, all on Atlanta +1.5 (card line: Bears −1.5). Atlanta lost by 8. Missed by 6.5.

The Formula: Net ratings Falcons 2.6, Bears −5.9 (nflverse play-by-play, Oct. 18, 2026). Follow The Money's case was the line moving from Falcons +3.5 to +1.5. Chicago led 21-7 at the half, and The Formula's gap never showed up on the field.

Atlanta's first drive of the second half died on fourth-and-3 at the Chicago 28 with an incompletion. Late in the third, Zachariah Branch fumbled a kickoff and Chicago recovered at the Atlanta 31. That became a Cairo Santos 50-yard field goal and a 31-7 lead.

Atlanta still had a way back at 31-23 with about three minutes left. A holding call erased a 9-yard completion on third-and-6. On third-and-16, Kyler Gordon strip-sacked Michael Penix Jr. and Chicago recovered at the Atlanta 28. That ended the cover.
Missed: the Cover Writer and The Formula on Baltimore −3 (card line). Baltimore lost by 3. Missed by 6.
The Formula: Net ratings Ravens 1.8, Browns −9.6 (nflverse play-by-play, Oct. 18, 2026). The Ravens scored 10 points in the first quarter and none after it.

The game turned in about 90 seconds early in the fourth quarter. Tyler Loop missed a 49-yard field goal wide left at 10-3. On Baltimore's next snap, Derrick Henry fumbled and Cleveland recovered at the Baltimore 35. Audric Estime scored from 2 yards out to tie it 10-10 with 8:33 left. From there Baltimore needed to win by four, and it never scored again.

The finish was a penalty story. With 2 seconds left, Andre Szmyt's 42-yard try was blocked, but the Ravens were flagged for offside on the play, so the block did not count. Szmyt made the next one from 37.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 44.5 (card total). The final total was 46. Missed by 1.5.

The card projected a 44-point game, and the game went right up to the number. With 2:03 left it was 23-20, a 43-point game. Indianapolis then went backward: a sack on third-and-10, then an incompletion on fourth-and-17 from its own 31. That handed Tennessee the ball at the Colts' 31, and Joey Slye's 44-yard field goal with 43 seconds left made it 46.
No projection includes a blocked punt returned for a touchdown, and this game had one. J. Chestnut blocked it and Oluwafemi Oladejo returned it 14 yards for a 20-13 lead with 10:17 left.
Missed: the Cover Writer on New England −7.5 and on Under 43.5 (card lines). The Patriots won by 7, so the side missed by 0.5. The total was 45, so the Under missed by 1.5.
The card named this exact risk before kickoff: "A Patriots win by exactly 7 lands on the Jets' side, which is why the hook matters here." A win by exactly 7 is what happened.

Three plays did it. First, Andy Borregales missed the extra point after Hunter Henry's 7-yard touchdown with 14:10 left, so it was 23-13 instead of 24-13. Second, with 1:14 left New England had fourth-and-1 at the Jets' 4, took a delay-of-game penalty, and kicked a 27-yard field goal for 26-16. Third, on the Jets' last drive, K. Byard was called for interference, 17 yards, to the New England 18 with 46 seconds left. Jason Sanders kicked a 36-yarder with 32 seconds left.
That one kick made it a 7-point game and a 45-point game. It flipped the side and pushed the total over at the same time.
Missed: the Cover Writer on New York +1.5 and on Under 46 (card lines). The Giants lost by 7, so the side missed by 5.5. The total was 61, so the Under missed by 15.

The card saw a coin flip. The Formula: Net ratings Giants −11.9, Saints −10.3 (nflverse play-by-play, Oct. 18, 2026). It was 10-10 at the half, and then New Orleans scored 24 straight points. Tyler Shough threw a 31-yard touchdown to Alvin Kamara and ran one in from a yard out. Daniel Carlson added a 51-yard field goal. Jameis Winston threw two interceptions in that stretch, and the second set up Shough's 18-yard touchdown to Chris Olave for 34-10. J.J. McCarthy took the Giants' snaps from there.

The Under was still alive at 44 points with 11:31 left. Then the Giants scored 17 points in the final 11 minutes. Tyrone Tracy Jr.'s 5-yard touchdown run plus McCarthy's two-point throw to Isaiah Likely made it 52 with 7:00 left, and the Under was gone.

The side had one last chance. McCarthy drove the Giants from their own 29 to the Saints' 14 in 45 seconds. On fourth-and-1 with 12 seconds left, his throw for Likely fell incomplete. A touchdown and the extra point there would have tied the game, and New York +1.5 would have been safe.

Missed: the Cover Writer and The Formula on Tampa Bay +2.5 (card line: Steelers −2.5), missed by 4.5. Also the Cover Writer and Follow The Money on Under 38.5 (card total). The final total was 45, missed by 6.5.

The Formula had two nearly identical teams. The Formula: Net ratings Steelers −6.6, Buccaneers −6.8 (nflverse play-by-play, Oct. 18, 2026). Follow The Money had the total falling from 40.5 to 38.5. At the end of regulation, both were still alive.

Tampa Bay led 16-3 going into the fourth quarter. Pittsburgh's touchdown drive early in the fourth got a 15-yard roughing-the-passer call on C. Kancey and ended in Darnell Washington's 5-yard touchdown. Later, on third-and-5, a 12-yard interference call on J. Parrish kept alive the drive that ended with Chris Boswell's 58-yard field goal to tie it 16-16.

On Tampa Bay's second snap after the kickoff, J. Dean intercepted Jalon Daniels and returned it 40 yards to the Tampa Bay 3. Pittsburgh settled for Boswell's 20-yarder. Chase McLaughlin's 53-yard field goal with 8 seconds left tied it 19-19. At the end of regulation, Tampa Bay +2.5 was covering and the total was 38, half a point under.
Overtime took both. Pittsburgh went 70 yards in 12 plays, and Aaron Rodgers hit Germie Bernard for a 6-yard touchdown with 3:15 left in the extra period. One throw flipped the side and the total.
Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches, all on Los Angeles −12.5 (card line). The Rams lost outright. Missed by 14.5.
Four of the five cards agreed on the Rams, and Follow The Money showed no side. The Formula: Net ratings Rams 6.1, Cardinals −8.9 (nflverse play-by-play, Oct. 18, 2026).

The Rams scored one touchdown in the first 59 minutes. Chad Ryland kicked six field goals. Los Angeles was stopped on fourth-and-1 at the Arizona 27 in the third quarter. In the fourth, a 26-yard interference call on K. Clark moved the Rams to the Arizona 19, and two plays later T. Higbee fumbled and Arizona recovered at its 25. The Rams failed again on fourth-and-8 at the Arizona 44 with 3:23 left.

Colby Parkinson was ruled down at the 1, replay reversed it to a 6-yard touchdown, and the Rams led 16-15 with 47 seconds left. On Arizona's first snap after the kickoff, J. Brissett hit J. Brooks for 21 yards and J. Wallace was flagged 15 more for unnecessary roughness, to the Rams' 29. That penalty put Arizona in field-goal range, and Ryland made the 43-yarder as time expired.
Missed: the Cover Writer and Follow The Money on Los Angeles +7.5 (card line: Chiefs −7.5). Kansas City won by 16. Missed by 8.5.
Also missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on Over 41.5 (card total). The total was 28. Missed by 13.5.

An honest note on the side. Four of the five cards projected Kansas City 27, Los Angeles 19, an 8-point Chiefs win that covers the 7.5. The Cover Writer's card read Chiefs 26, Chargers 19, a 7-point margin, and that put the Cover Writer's side on the Chargers, against four of the five cards. Follow The Money's own case was the line dropping from Chiefs −8.5 to −7.5.

The Chargers' best chance came in the third quarter. They had first-and-goal at the Kansas City 1, and a holding call on J. Slaughter pushed them back. They settled for a 30-yard field goal and trailed 19-6. Their last drive ended on fourth-and-5 at the Kansas City 8 with a minute left.

The Over needed 42 points and lost points at both ends. Harrison Butker's extra point failed after Kenneth Walker III's 33-yard touchdown run. Kansas City was stopped on fourth-and-goal at the Chargers' 1 in the third quarter. Butker missed a 52-yard try wide right in the fourth. Add the Chargers' red-zone holding call and the 46-point projection on four of the cards ended up at 28.
Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches, all on Buffalo −5.5 (card line). Buffalo won by 3. Missed by 2.5.
Four of the five handicapper cards were on Buffalo. The Formula: Net ratings Bills 5.4, Raiders −9.9 (nflverse play-by-play, Oct. 18, 2026).

Buffalo led 33-23 after Tyler Bass's 38-yard field goal with 1:56 left. That was covering by 4.5. On the next drive, a 22-yard interference call on D. Alford moved Las Vegas to the Buffalo 44, and on the next play Kirk Cousins threw a 44-yard touchdown to Tre Tucker with 1:32 left. Buffalo recovered the onside kick, but the cover was already gone.

Buffalo also had a touchdown taken away. In the third quarter, an 18-yard touchdown throw to D. Kincaid on fourth-and-2 was wiped out by a holding call on O. Torrence, and the Bills settled for a 47-yard field goal.
Missed: In The Trenches on Dallas +1.5 (card line: Packers −1.5). Dallas lost by 10. Missed by 8.5. Also Follow The Money on Over 53.5 (card total). The total was 36. Missed by 17.5.

In The Trenches' case was the Green Bay run game, 1.92 yards a carry below what Dallas allows. Green Bay led 17-0 at the half. Down 23-7, Dallas drove to the Green Bay 14 and threw incomplete on fourth-and-11 with 5:05 left. Dallas scored again with 44 seconds left, on Ryan Flournoy's 6-yard catch, and the two-point try failed.
Follow The Money's case was the total rising from 52.5 to 53.5. The teams had 27 points through three quarters and 36 at the end.

Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula and Letdown Watch on Mississippi State +17.5 (card line: LSU −17.5). Mississippi State lost by 31. Missed by 13.5. The Cover Writer projected LSU 34, Mississippi State 18.

The Cover Writer expected LSU's missing linebackers and Mississippi State's extra week of rest to keep this from getting out of hand. With redshirt freshman Parker "Billy" Puckett at quarterback in place of Kamario Taylor, Mississippi State did not score. Sam Leavitt's third touchdown throw, 17 yards to Jackson Harris with 6:12 left in the first half, made it 21-0, and the margin never came back inside 17.5. Mississippi State turned it over on downs at the LSU 28 and the LSU 30 in the fourth quarter.
Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on Texas −11.5 (card line). Texas lost by 3. Missed by 14.5. The Cover Writer projected Texas 34, Florida 14.

The Cover Writer's case was Texas's defense against a Florida team starting a first-time quarterback, Tramell Jones Jr. Jones threw for two touchdowns to Lacota Dippre, and Florida led 20-17 in the fourth quarter. The moment that ended it came with 8:34 left: Arch Manning was stopped for a 3-yard loss on fourth down at the Texas 45. Florida scored from there, Jadan Baugh's 11-yard run for 27-17.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 50.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 48). The final total was 51. Missed by 0.5.
The Under was alive until 4:21 was left. Cam Coleman's 9-yard touchdown catch from Manning made it 51 points, half a point over.
Missed: Letdown Watch on Texas A&M −46.5 (card line). Texas A&M won by 41. Missed by 5.5.

Texas A&M led 34-0 after three quarters and needed to win by 47. Aaron Gregory's 12-yard touchdown catch from Brady Hart with 5:47 left made it 41-0, and that was the last score. The Citadel missed a 47-yard field goal with 1:13 left.
Missed: Follow The Money and In The Trenches on Georgia −19.5 (card line). Georgia lost by 3. Missed by 22.5.

Auburn led 24-14 after three quarters and won outright. Georgia's last real chance ended when Gunner Stockton fumbled near midfield with 58 seconds left; C. Sigler forced it and S. Smith-Reed recovered for Auburn.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 49.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 47). The final total was 51. Missed by 1.5.

The Under held until the last play. It was 24-24, a 48-point game, when Georgia was flagged for roughing the passer by G. Harris Jr. with 15 seconds left, 15 yards to the Georgia 19. Alex McPherson's 34-yard field goal on the final play made it 51.

Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on Missouri +5.5 (card line: Ole Miss −5.5). Missouri lost by 28. Missed by 22.5. The Cover Writer projected Ole Miss 31, Missouri 26.

The Cover Writer expected Missouri's defense and its running game to keep it close all the way. Trinidad Chambliss threw touchdowns of 10, 21 and 17 yards in the first half, and Missouri never scored again after its opening field goal. Its last drive ended with L. Barnes' interception at the Ole Miss 1.
Missed: the Cover Writer and Letdown Watch on Alabama −7.5 (card line). Alabama lost by 16. Missed by 23.5. The Cover Writer projected Alabama 28, Tennessee 20.

The Cover Writer's case was Alabama's offense and defense against a Tennessee quarterback, George MacIntyre, making his second career start. Tennessee won by 16. Cooper Ranvier kicked four first-half field goals, and DeSean Bishop scored on two 5-yard runs. Alabama's last drive ended with an interception by K. Lee in the end zone.
Missed: Follow The Money and In The Trenches on Vanderbilt −6 (card line). Vanderbilt lost by 10. Missed by 16.
Arkansas led 28-21 after Cam Settles' 3-yard run with 9 seconds left in the third. Vanderbilt's best drive of the fourth went 63 yards in 14 plays and ended with an interception by M. Mitchell.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 50.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 50). The final total was 52. Missed by 1.5.
The total was 49 with 24 seconds left. Max Gilbert's 39-yard field goal made it 52.
Missed: Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on Oklahoma −6.5 (card line). Oklahoma lost by 8. Missed by 14.5.

Kentucky won outright. Willie Rodriguez's 12-yard touchdown catch from Kenny Minchey put Kentucky ahead 14-13 with 12:53 left, and Jordan Castell returned an interception 41 yards for a touchdown with 1:17 left.

Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch, Follow The Money and In The Trenches on Cincinnati +1.5 (card line: West Virginia −1.5). Cincinnati lost by 3. Missed by 1.5. The Cover Writer projected Cincinnati 34, West Virginia 33.

Everyone on the card was on Cincinnati, and the Cover Writer's own line was "One late stop should settle it." Nobody stopped anybody. The game was tied six times, each time after Cincinnati scored and West Virginia answered. Cam Cook's 40-yard touchdown catch from Michael Hawkins Jr. tied it 42-42 with 3:44 left. At 42-42, Cincinnati +1.5 was covering. Jack Cassidy's 35-yard field goal as time expired ended that.
Missed: Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on Kansas +3.5 (card line: Kansas State −3.5). Kansas lost by 11. Missed by 7.5.

Kansas led 24-18 in the third. Two fourth-quarter plays hurt it most. Isaiah Marshall was intercepted near the end zone by L. Bartley with 10:02 left, and Kansas State scored on its next possession, Jaron Tibbs' 9-yard catch from Avery Johnson for 32-24, a drive helped by a Kansas face-mask penalty. Then Marshall broke a 46-yard touchdown run, and another Kansas face-mask penalty took it off the board. That touchdown would have made it 32-30 before the extra point.
Missed: Follow The Money and In The Trenches on Arizona State +15.5 (card line: Texas Tech −15.5). Arizona State lost by 28. Missed by 12.5.
Texas Tech led 43-10 at the half. It started with Ben Roberts' 24-yard interception return, and J'Koby Williams added touchdown runs of 62 and 38 yards.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 49.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 47). The final total was 78. Missed by 28.5.

The Under rested on Texas Tech's defense. The defense scored, and the offense scored 46 more. The total passed 49.5 before halftime, on Coy Eakin's 11-yard catch from Will Hammond with 31 seconds left in the second quarter. The final total was 78.
Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula and In The Trenches on Baylor −5.5 (card line). Baylor lost by 11. Missed by 16.5. The Cover Writer projected Baylor 27, TCU 20.
The Cover Writer's case was Baylor playing at home and TCU missing two offensive linemen. Baylor scored two field goals all night. Its last two drives both ended on fourth-down incompletions.
Missed: the Cover Writer and Follow The Money on Notre Dame −10.5 (card line). Notre Dame lost by 4. Missed by 14.5. The Cover Writer projected Notre Dame 28, BYU 17.
BYU won outright. Notre Dame led 24-21 after Jonaz Walton's 3-yard run and two-point run with 9:31 left. Bear Bachmeier's 6-yard touchdown throw to Walker Lyons with 1:47 left won it.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 47.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 45). The final total was 52. Missed by 4.5.
Lyons' touchdown also took the total from 45 to 52.
Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula, Follow The Money and In The Trenches on Houston −4.5 (card line). Houston won by 3. Missed by 1.5. The Cover Writer projected Houston 36, Oklahoma State 29.
Houston led 35-25 after Koby Young's 48-yard catch with 9:48 left. Drew Mestemaker's 8-yard touchdown throw to Justin Bowick with 4:54 left cut it to 3, and nobody scored after that.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Utah −14.5 (card line). Utah won by 3. Missed by 11.5. The Cover Writer projected Utah 32, Colorado 17.

The Cover Writer's pick went against all five handicappers, who all had Colorado. Colorado scored 17 straight points in the third quarter to lead 17-13. Utah took the lead back but never led by 15: Braden Pegan's 6-yard catch from Devon Dampier with 3:43 left made it 27-17, and Colorado answered.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 49.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 49). The final total was 51. Missed by 1.5.
The Under stood at 44 points with 1:21 left. DeAndre Moore Jr.'s 2-yard touchdown catch from Isaac Wilson made it 51.
Missed: Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on Clemson −43.5 (card line). Clemson won by 37. Missed by 6.5.
Clemson led 34-0 at the half and scored 3 more points. Nolan Hauser's 44-yard field goal early in the fourth was the last score. Clemson's last drive ended on downs at the Charleston Southern 27.
Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula and In The Trenches on Pittsburgh −6.5 (card line). Pittsburgh lost by 6. Missed by 12.5. The Cover Writer projected Pittsburgh 24, Boston College 15.

The Cover Writer's case was Pitt's defense making up for a true freshman quarterback's first start. Pitt led 12-0 early, then Boston College scored 21 straight. The last of those, Mason McKenzie's 69-yard touchdown throw to Landon Wright 46 seconds into the second half, made it 21-12. Pitt never got closer than 3.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 42.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 39). The final total was 48. Missed by 5.5.
The Under was gone with 13:02 left, when Evan Dickens' 1-yard run made it 45 points. The final total was 48.
Missed: The Formula, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on Georgia Tech +8.5 (card line: Virginia Tech −8.5). Georgia Tech lost by 10. Missed by 1.5.

Georgia Tech trailed 34-17 and got within 10, which was not enough. The key play: Aidan Birr missed a 32-yard field goal with 10:26 left. Jaiven Plummer's 6-yard touchdown catch with 5:20 left then made it 34-24. Had Birr's kick been good, that touchdown would have left a 7-point game.
Missed: Next Man Up, Follow The Money and In The Trenches on Duke −3 (card line). Duke lost by 4. Missed by 7.

Duke rallied from 17-0 and led 20-17 after Nate Sheppard's 7-yard catch from Walker Eget with 4:39 left. Jaylen McGill's 24-yard touchdown run with 1:53 left put North Carolina back in front, and K. Dopson III intercepted Eget at the North Carolina 15 with 19 seconds left.
Missed: the Cover Writer, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on Miami −20.5 (card line). Miami won by 8. Missed by 12.5. The Cover Writer projected Miami 41, Florida State 19.

Florida State led 21-14 after three quarters and did not go away. Duce Robinson's 75-yard touchdown catch from Ashton Daniels tied it 28-28 with 2:39 left. Miami won in the second overtime on Malachi Toney's 3-yard touchdown catch, and Toney threw for the two points himself.
Missed: Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on Stanford −34.5 (card line). Stanford won by 27. Missed by 7.5.

Stanford led 34-0 after Micah Ford's 81-yard run early in the fourth, and the extra point failed. That left Stanford exactly 34 points ahead, half a point short. Elon's Kamerin McDowell-Moore then scored on an 18-yard run, and Stanford's last scoring chance ended with a fumble at the Elon 1 that went through the end zone for a touchback.
Missed: Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on Louisville −14.5 (card line). Louisville won by 8. Missed by 6.5.

Syracuse, playing its third quarterback option, led 23-21 in the second quarter and trailed only 28-26 with 12:45 left. Keyjuan Brown's 5-yard run with 7:34 left made it 34-26, and the extra point failed. Syracuse's last two drives ended on downs, but an 8-point loss covers 14.5.
Missed: Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on California +10 (card line: Wake Forest −10). California lost by 34. Missed by 24.
Wake Forest led 41-0 after three quarters. Dominick Barry caught three of Gio Lopez's touchdown throws.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Over 53.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 54). The final total was 48. Missed by 5.5.
Wake Forest did its part with 41. California scored 7, on Mason Mini's 28-yard catch in the fourth, and its last drive ended on downs. The total was 48.

Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Follow The Money and In The Trenches on Indiana +3 (card line: Ohio State −3). Indiana lost by 4. Missed by 1. The Cover Writer projected Ohio State 26, Indiana 25.

Indiana needed to lose by 2 or fewer. Ohio State's two-point try failed after Jeremiah Smith's 38-yard touchdown catch, leaving it 19-7. Josh Hoover's 19-yard touchdown throw to Nick Marsh and a two-point throw to Turbo Richard made it 19-15 with 10:30 left. Indiana's last drive ended with a fourth-down incompletion for Marsh with 1:07 left.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Over 50.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 51). The final total was 34. Missed by 16.5.
The Cover Writer expected the offenses to win out. Two top-15 defenses held it to 34 points.

Missed: the Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on Northwestern −7 (card line). Northwestern won by 3. Missed by 4. The Cover Writer projected Northwestern 30, Michigan State 20.

Northwestern won on the last kick but never covered at any point. It trailed 21-13 in the fourth, tied it on Aidan Chiles' 1-yard run and two-point throw, blocked Michigan State's 33-yard field goal try with a minute left, and won on Jackson Kleather's 34-yarder with 2 seconds left. A 3-point win, 4 points short.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Over 49.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 50). The final total was 45. Missed by 4.5.
The game had two blocked field goals, a Kleather try in the second quarter and Michigan State's late one. The total was 45.
Missed: Next Man Up, Follow The Money and In The Trenches on Maryland −6 (card line). Maryland lost by 7. Missed by 13.

Tied 23-23 late in the third, Rutgers then scored two touchdowns: Clay Thevenin's 7-yard run and Antwan Raymond's 2-yard run for 37-23. Maryland's last drive ended on a fourth-down incompletion with 19 seconds left.
Missed: the Cover Writer on Under 55.5 (card total; the Cover Writer projected 53). The final total was 67. Missed by 11.5.
The total passed 55.5 on Raymond's touchdown with 4:03 left. The final total was 67. The card's forecast of gusts around 37 mph did not slow either offense.
Missed: Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on Michigan −6.5 (card line). Michigan won by 3. Missed by 3.5.

Michigan led 21-11 after Tommy Carr's 12-yard run with 2:58 left. On third-and-8 at the Michigan 34 with 1:18 left, Michigan was called for holding, a 10-yard penalty and a first down. On the next play Rocco Becht hit Chase Sowell for a 24-yard touchdown. Final 21-18.
